To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HSP72 protein is increased after damaging eccentric exercise in human skeletal muscle but remains exclusively cytosolic.

1) the amount of Hsp72 protein in human skeletal muscle is ~11.4 μMol/kg muscle wet weight, and 2) after eccentric exercise, HSP72 protein does not bind to SERCA in human muscle, and therefore the role of SERCA as a primary target of HSP72 in skeletal muscle remains unclear.

in human skeletal muscle HSP72 protein is not translocated from cytosol to membranes after eccentric and concentric contractions, and the total amount of HSP 72 protein increases 24 h after eccentric exercise.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the mechanisms of HSP72 upregulation and its translocation to membranes after physiological stress, and the findings of this study have important implications for our understanding of the function of HSP72 in skeletal muscle after eccentric exercise.
understanding HSP72 protein function in human skeletal muscle and how it responds to physiological stress.
the role of HSP72 in skeletal muscle protection and repair and suggests HSP72 may have a more limited role in skeletal muscle compared with other cell types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in total HSP 72 protein after ECC1 was not due to translocation of HSP72 from the cytosol to other cellular compartments.
HSP72 does increase in response to exercise stress but does not associate with membrane proteins in human skeletal muscle.
HSP72 protein is not involved in the protection of SERCA after eccentric contractions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HSP72 protein does not associate with key membrane proteins after damaging eccentric exercise in humans.
HSP72 is upregulated and/or translocated in a stressor-dependent manner and, in human skeletal muscle, HSP72 does so after heat, but not after eccentric exercise.

HSP72 protein is present in human skeletal muscle, is present in both Type I and II muscle fiber segments, is increased after damaging eccentric exercise and, unlike other forms and sites of stress, does not translocate to membranes and myofibrils.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the increase in total HSP70 protein content in human skeletal muscle after ECC1 is a consequence of increased protein synthesis and not a result of translocation from the cytosol to membranes/myofibers.

, despite a 2-fold increase in the amount of HSC70 protein, it does not appear to bind to SERCA in human muscle after damaging eccentric exercise, which is in contrast to what is observed in rodent models.

the HSP72 content in human skeletal muscle is very high and, in response to physiological exercise stress, the amount of total HSP72 increases, but the protein does not translocate to the membranes/myofibrillar fraction.
